chapters.title: Chapter 11 — In-, im-, il- and ir-
chapters.focus: in-, im-, il- and ir- meaning not
chapters.description: Our examples of words that start with in-, im-, il- or ir- to mean not, as in invisible.

meaning.definition: Not able to be seen.
meaning.example: The magician made the rabbit look invisible.

meaning.definition: Not having good manners.
meaning.example: It is impolite to talk with your mouth full.

meaning.definition: Not moving or doing anything much.
meaning.example: The sleepy cat stayed inactive all afternoon.

meaning.definition: Not happy to wait for something.
meaning.example: Mia grew impatient waiting for the bus.

meaning.definition: Not allowed by the law.
meaning.example: It is illegal to drive without a licence.

meaning.definition: Not perfect; having a small fault.
meaning.example: My drawing is imperfect, but I like it.

meaning.definition: Not able to happen or be done.
meaning.example: Flapping your arms to fly is impossible.

meaning.definition: Not following the usual pattern or shape.
meaning.example: The stone had an irregular shape.

meaning.definition: Not sensible; not following clear thinking.
meaning.example: Wearing a coat in a heatwave is illogical.

meaning.definition: Not careful or sensible about what you do.
meaning.example: Leaving the gate open was irresponsible.

chapters.title: Chapter 12 — Words ending -sure and -ture
chapters.description: Our examples of words ending in -sure or -ture, such as measure and picture.

meaning.definition: A drawing, painting or photograph.
meaning.example: She hung the picture on the wall.

meaning.definition: Plants, animals and the world outside that people have not made.
meaning.example: We walked through the woods to enjoy nature.

meaning.definition: The time that is still to come.
meaning.example: I want to be a vet in the future.

meaning.definition: To find out how big, long or heavy something is.
meaning.example: Please measure the table with a ruler.

meaning.definition: Gold, jewels or other valuable things.
meaning.example: The pirates buried the treasure on the island.

meaning.definition: A feeling of happiness and enjoyment.
meaning.example: Reading gives me great pleasure.

meaning.definition: Any living animal.
meaning.example: A tiny creature crept under the leaf.

meaning.definition: Different things stirred or put together.
meaning.example: Stir the mixture until it is smooth.

meaning.definition: An exciting journey or experience.
meaning.example: Our camping trip was a big adventure.

meaning.definition: Things like chairs, tables and beds in a room.
meaning.example: We bought new furniture for the lounge.

chapters.title: Chapter 13 — The -sion sound
chapters.description: Our examples of words ending in -sion that sound like zhun, such as television and decision.

meaning.definition: The ability to see.
meaning.example: The optician checked my vision.

meaning.definition: A choice you make after thinking.
meaning.example: We made a decision to go swimming.

meaning.definition: Sharing or splitting a number into equal groups.
meaning.example: Division is the opposite of multiplication.

meaning.definition: A screen that shows programmes and films.
meaning.example: We watched a funny film on television.

meaning.definition: Not being sure what is happening or what to do.
meaning.example: There was confusion when the lights went out.

meaning.definition: A sudden, loud burst, like a firework.
meaning.example: We heard a loud explosion of fireworks.

meaning.definition: The end of something, or what you decide after thinking.
meaning.example: The story has a happy conclusion.

meaning.definition: When two moving things crash into each other.
meaning.example: The two bumper cars had a gentle collision.

meaning.definition: Watching over people to keep them safe.
meaning.example: Children may only swim with adult supervision.

meaning.definition: Looking over work again to learn it well.
meaning.example: Revision helped me learn my spellings.

chapters.title: Chapter 14 — The -ous ending
chapters.description: Our examples of describing words that end in -ous, such as nervous and dangerous.

meaning.definition: A little worried or afraid about something.
meaning.example: Sam felt nervous before the school play.

meaning.definition: Not joking; important and needing care.
meaning.example: Dad had a serious look on his face.

meaning.definition: Keen to find out or learn about things.
meaning.example: The curious puppy sniffed every corner.

meaning.definition: Wanting something that someone else has.
meaning.example: Ben felt jealous of his friend's new bike.

meaning.definition: Happy to give or share with others.
meaning.example: My gran is generous with her biscuits.

meaning.definition: Likely to cause harm.
meaning.example: The icy path was dangerous to walk on.

meaning.definition: Very, very big.
meaning.example: An enormous whale swam past the boat.

meaning.definition: Keen to try new and exciting things.
meaning.example: My adventurous sister always climbs to the very top.

meaning.definition: Strange and hard to explain.
meaning.example: A mysterious box appeared on the doorstep.

meaning.definition: So silly that it makes you laugh.
meaning.example: He wore a ridiculous hat to the party.

chapters.title: Chapter 15 — ch, gue, que and sc
chapters.focus: ch for k and sh, gue, que and sc
chapters.description: Our examples of spellings borrowed from other languages, such as chorus, tongue, unique and science.

meaning.definition: A shop or person that gives out medicines.
meaning.example: Mum went to the chemist for some plasters.

meaning.definition: A group of people singing together.
meaning.example: The chorus sang loudly at the concert.

meaning.definition: A person who cooks food as a job.
meaning.example: The chef baked a huge chocolate cake.

meaning.definition: Something with moving parts that does a job.
meaning.example: The machine washed our muddy clothes.

meaning.definition: The part inside your mouth that helps you taste.
meaning.example: The lolly turned my tongue bright blue.

meaning.definition: One of a kind; like no other.
meaning.example: Every snowflake is unique.

meaning.definition: Learning about the world through looking and testing.
meaning.example: In science we grew beans in pots.

meaning.definition: A tool with two blades for cutting paper.
meaning.example: Please pass me the scissors and glue.

meaning.definition: A person or animal in a story.
meaning.example: My favourite character in the book is a fox.

meaning.definition: A special way of doing something well.
meaning.example: The teacher showed us a new painting technique.
